newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe budget deficit seen at 8.9 pct in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe budget deficit seen at 8.9 pct in 1997/98.

text.p: Zimbabwe's budget deficit is expected to rise to 8.9 percent of gross domestic product in the 1997/98 fiscal year from 7.1 percent in 1996/97, Finance Minister Herbert Murerwa said on Thursday.
He said in his budget speech the estimate excluded grants and privatisation proceeds. If these were included, the deficit would be lower at 7.8 percent of GDP.
"The 1997/98 deficit stands at Z$15 billion excluding grants and privatisation proceeds which represents 8.9 percent, which is higher than 7.1 percent of GDP achieved in 1996/97," Murerwa said.

He said the lower than forecast 1996/97 deficit was largely due to increased revenue collection. Two weeks ago, Murerwa pegged the 1996/97 deficit at 10.3 percent of GDP, off a government-set target of 8.5 percent.
